title: Monetary Policy Report, July 13, 2018
summary: The Federal Reserve submitted its quarterly Monetary Policy Report to Congress on July 13, 2018, reaffirming its dual mandate: maximum employment and price stability (2% inflation target measured by PCE). Chairman Jerome H. Powell transmitted the report, which outlines the FOMC's commitment to a symmetric inflation goal and the Committee's balanced approach when employment and inflation objectives conflict. The report references the median FOMC estimate of 4.6% as the longer-run normal unemployment rate. Note: Source text captured only the front matter and statement of longer-run goals; substantive economic analysis (Parts 1-3) was truncated and unavailable.
key_points: The FOMC reaffirms its 2% inflation target measured by annual change in the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index
The Committee would be concerned if inflation were running persistently above or below the 2% objective, indicating a symmetric policy stance
Median FOMC participant estimate of the longer-run normal rate of unemployment is 4.6 percent
Maximum employment is largely determined by nonmonetary factors and cannot be specified as a fixed goal
Monetary policy actions influence economic activity and prices with a lag, requiring the Committee to consider medium-term outlook and balance of risks
The Committee intends to reaffirm its policy principles and make adjustments at its annual organizational meeting each January
The report notes data available through July 11, 2018 for daily data and June 2018 for monthly data
why_it_matters: This quarterly report establishes the foundational policy framework and mandate interpretation that guided Fed decision-making in mid-2018. For macro analysis, it provides the official baseline for how the FOMC thinks about the employment-inflation tradeoff, the symmetric nature of its inflation target, and the uncertainty inherent in estimating maximum employment. Market participants use these documents to understand the Fed's reaction function and policy strategy. [Note: Substantive economic analysis and projections from Parts 1-3 of the report are not available in the source text for verification.]
macro_context: The report discusses the Fed's understanding of how monetary policy transmits to the real economy through lagged effects, and how the Committee balances employment deviations against inflation deviations when objectives conflict. This framework was relevant to understanding policy decisions during the 2018 tightening cycle.
